# gh-1106: SM: fork silent-update must escalate token on 'workflows' permission rejection instead of guest-parking

## Description

## Goal — fork silent-update survives `workflows`-permission rejection (v1)
One sentence: **an approved fork PR whose update-from-main touches `.github/workflows/*` gets its branch updated and merged by the SM instead of parking guest-style forever.**

Today the SM's fork silent-update (`js/smAgent.js` ~2380–2440) pushes the `main` merge into the fork head with `silentToken` (= the caller's `github.token`, `github-actions[bot]`). `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files (no `workflows` permission exists for it, `permissions:` cannot grant it). As soon as `main` has a workflow-file change the fork branch lacks, every push is rejected, `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` counts it as "maintainer edits revoked", and after 3 ticks the PR is parked guest-style with `validation_failed`, which then holds because "the head predates the park event (no new push since)". Deadlock: no push → park holds → no push.

Live case: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591 (fork `YuryBY`, `maintainerCanModify=true`, APPROVED, BEHIND), ticks 2026-10-19 17:16/17:17:
```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> fix/android-dap-home-sandbox (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` without `workflows` permission)
❌ pr-1591 fork silent-update parked guest-style after 3 consecutive push failures (gh-1070 AC3)
🅿️ pr-1591 validation_failed holds — the head predates the park event (no new push since)
```

## Why this framing
- Retracted: "maintainer edits were revoked" — the misdiagnosis gh-1070 AC3 applies to *every* push failure. This rejection is a token-capability fact, not an author decision, and it is deterministic (retrying with the same token can never succeed).
- Retracted: fixing in workflow YAML. `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml` already deliver both `silentToken` and `sourceToken`; the decision belongs to the engine.

## Architecture
Subject of every action = **the fork PR head branch** (`head.repo.full_name`:`head.ref`), never the base repo.

```
silent push (silentToken) ──ok──▶ done (no CI event, as today)
        │ rejected
        ▼ classify stderr tail
  workflows-permission? ──no──▶ existing gh-1070 AC3 trail (unchanged)
        │ yes
        ▼
  escalated push (sourceToken: App installation token or PAT) ──ok──▶ head moved;
        │                                                      CI fires normally (acceptable: head changed, revalidation is required anyway)
        │ rejected (escalation token also lacks workflow write)
        ▼
  park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token" (actionable, not "edits revoked"); not counted toward the 3-strike trail
```
Invariants:
- Same token-in-env pattern as today: `forkPushTokenUrl` keeps `${GH_TOKEN}` in the URL; the escalation only swaps env `GH_TOKEN` and restores it in `finally`. The token never appears in script source or logs.
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- The same classification + escalation applies to the non-fork path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (`js/common/smProvider.js` ~839) for base-repo branches.
- A `validation_failed` park created by a workflows-permission rejection is lifted when the escalated push moves the head (the head now post-dates the park).

## Capability surface (tokens available to the tick)
| Token | Source | Workflow-file write | Push fires CI | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silentToken` | `github.token` | **never** (platform fact) | no | default silent update (core, unchanged) |
| App installation token | `create-github-app-token` (APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY) | only if App has *Workflows: write* | yes | escalation (core) |
| `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT | secret | only with `workflow` scope | yes | escalation fallback when no App (core) |
Excluded: requesting permissions at runtime (impossible); rewriting the merge to skip workflow files (corrupts the branch).

Pinned platform facts (each with +/- test via stderr fixtures): `GITHUB_TOKEN` push touching `.github/workflows/**` is rejected; same push with workflow-capable token succeeds; push not touching workflows succeeds with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Security
- Escalation token is a write token to a **fork** owned by a third party, used only under `maintainerCanModify=true` (existing gate, unchanged).
- Never log the token; stderr tail stays redacted (existing redaction).
- Escalation pushes only the SM-built merge commit of `main` into head — no author content is executed before the push.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- **AC2** — that rejection does **not** increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- **AC3** — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- **AC4** — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- **AC5** — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- **AC6** — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- **AC7** — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

## Test plan
- `UT-1..5` in `js/unit-tests` with stderr fixtures (the exact #1591 line + OAuth-scope variant + unrelated rejection).
- `IT-1/2` SM tick harness with stubbed `cli_execute_command`: first push rejected → second with swapped env succeeds → head moves.
- `REG-1` existing gh-1070 / gh-1074 fork tests unchanged and green.
- Red REG blocks merge even if UT/IT are green.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — no App and PAT lacks `workflow` scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- **E2** — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- **E3** — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- **E4** — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

## Non-goals
- Changing tokens wired in `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml`.
- Auto-unparking PRs parked by genuine maintainer-edit revocation.

## Open questions
- Does the fa App have *Workflows: write*? If not: grant it, or rely on PAT `workflow` scope.

## References
- IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591; gh-1070 AC3, gh-1074 (fork silent-update trail); #687 (silent token); awf#52 (App token).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real

     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false

   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,

# gh-1106: SM: fork silent-update must escalate token on 'workflows' permission rejection instead of guest-parking

## Description

## Goal — fork silent-update survives `workflows`-permission rejection (v1)
One sentence: **an approved fork PR whose update-from-main touches `.github/workflows/*` gets its branch updated and merged by the SM instead of parking guest-style forever.**

Today the SM's fork silent-update (`js/smAgent.js` ~2380–2440) pushes the `main` merge into the fork head with `silentToken` (= the caller's `github.token`, `github-actions[bot]`). `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files (no `workflows` permission exists for it, `permissions:` cannot grant it). As soon as `main` has a workflow-file change the fork branch lacks, every push is rejected, `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` counts it as "maintainer edits revoked", and after 3 ticks the PR is parked guest-style with `validation_failed`, which then holds because "the head predates the park event (no new push since)". Deadlock: no push → park holds → no push.

Live case: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591 (fork `YuryBY`, `maintainerCanModify=true`, APPROVED, BEHIND), ticks 2026-10-19 17:16/17:17:
```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> fix/android-dap-home-sandbox (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` without `workflows` permission)
❌ pr-1591 fork silent-update parked guest-style after 3 consecutive push failures (gh-1070 AC3)
🅿️ pr-1591 validation_failed holds — the head predates the park event (no new push since)
```

## Why this framing
- Retracted: "maintainer edits were revoked" — the misdiagnosis gh-1070 AC3 applies to *every* push failure. This rejection is a token-capability fact, not an author decision, and it is deterministic (retrying with the same token can never succeed).
- Retracted: fixing in workflow YAML. `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml` already deliver both `silentToken` and `sourceToken`; the decision belongs to the engine.

## Architecture
Subject of every action = **the fork PR head branch** (`head.repo.full_name`:`head.ref`), never the base repo.

```
silent push (silentToken) ──ok──▶ done (no CI event, as today)
        │ rejected
        ▼ classify stderr tail
  workflows-permission? ──no──▶ existing gh-1070 AC3 trail (unchanged)
        │ yes
        ▼
  escalated push (sourceToken: App installation token or PAT) ──ok──▶ head moved;
        │                                                      CI fires normally (acceptable: head changed, revalidation is required anyway)
        │ rejected (escalation token also lacks workflow write)
        ▼
  park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token" (actionable, not "edits revoked"); not counted toward the 3-strike trail
```
Invariants:
- Same token-in-env pattern as today: `forkPushTokenUrl` keeps `${GH_TOKEN}` in the URL; the escalation only swaps env `GH_TOKEN` and restores it in `finally`. The token never appears in script source or logs.
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- The same classification + escalation applies to the non-fork path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (`js/common/smProvider.js` ~839) for base-repo branches.
- A `validation_failed` park created by a workflows-permission rejection is lifted when the escalated push moves the head (the head now post-dates the park).

## Capability surface (tokens available to the tick)
| Token | Source | Workflow-file write | Push fires CI | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silentToken` | `github.token` | **never** (platform fact) | no | default silent update (core, unchanged) |
| App installation token | `create-github-app-token` (APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY) | only if App has *Workflows: write* | yes | escalation (core) |
| `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT | secret | only with `workflow` scope | yes | escalation fallback when no App (core) |
Excluded: requesting permissions at runtime (impossible); rewriting the merge to skip workflow files (corrupts the branch).

Pinned platform facts (each with +/- test via stderr fixtures): `GITHUB_TOKEN` push touching `.github/workflows/**` is rejected; same push with workflow-capable token succeeds; push not touching workflows succeeds with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Security
- Escalation token is a write token to a **fork** owned by a third party, used only under `maintainerCanModify=true` (existing gate, unchanged).
- Never log the token; stderr tail stays redacted (existing redaction).
- Escalation pushes only the SM-built merge commit of `main` into head — no author content is executed before the push.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- **AC2** — that rejection does **not** increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- **AC3** — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- **AC4** — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- **AC5** — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- **AC6** — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- **AC7** — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

## Test plan
- `UT-1..5` in `js/unit-tests` with stderr fixtures (the exact #1591 line + OAuth-scope variant + unrelated rejection).
- `IT-1/2` SM tick harness with stubbed `cli_execute_command`: first push rejected → second with swapped env succeeds → head moves.
- `REG-1` existing gh-1070 / gh-1074 fork tests unchanged and green.
- Red REG blocks merge even if UT/IT are green.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — no App and PAT lacks `workflow` scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- **E2** — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- **E3** — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- **E4** — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

## Non-goals
- Changing tokens wired in `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml`.
- Auto-unparking PRs parked by genuine maintainer-edit revocation.

## Open questions
- Does the fa App have *Workflows: write*? If not: grant it, or rely on PAT `workflow` scope.

## References
- IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591; gh-1070 AC3, gh-1074 (fork silent-update trail); #687 (silent token); awf#52 (App token).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# gh-1106: SM: fork silent-update must escalate token on 'workflows' permission rejection instead of guest-parking

## Description

## Goal — fork silent-update survives `workflows`-permission rejection (v1)
One sentence: **an approved fork PR whose update-from-main touches `.github/workflows/*` gets its branch updated and merged by the SM instead of parking guest-style forever.**

Today the SM's fork silent-update (`js/smAgent.js` ~2380–2440) pushes the `main` merge into the fork head with `silentToken` (= the caller's `github.token`, `github-actions[bot]`). `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files (no `workflows` permission exists for it, `permissions:` cannot grant it). As soon as `main` has a workflow-file change the fork branch lacks, every push is rejected, `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` counts it as "maintainer edits revoked", and after 3 ticks the PR is parked guest-style with `validation_failed`, which then holds because "the head predates the park event (no new push since)". Deadlock: no push → park holds → no push.

Live case: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591 (fork `YuryBY`, `maintainerCanModify=true`, APPROVED, BEHIND), ticks 2026-10-19 17:16/17:17:
```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> fix/android-dap-home-sandbox (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` without `workflows` permission)
❌ pr-1591 fork silent-update parked guest-style after 3 consecutive push failures (gh-1070 AC3)
🅿️ pr-1591 validation_failed holds — the head predates the park event (no new push since)
```

## Why this framing
- Retracted: "maintainer edits were revoked" — the misdiagnosis gh-1070 AC3 applies to *every* push failure. This rejection is a token-capability fact, not an author decision, and it is deterministic (retrying with the same token can never succeed).
- Retracted: fixing in workflow YAML. `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml` already deliver both `silentToken` and `sourceToken`; the decision belongs to the engine.

## Architecture
Subject of every action = **the fork PR head branch** (`head.repo.full_name`:`head.ref`), never the base repo.

```
silent push (silentToken) ──ok──▶ done (no CI event, as today)
        │ rejected
        ▼ classify stderr tail
  workflows-permission? ──no──▶ existing gh-1070 AC3 trail (unchanged)
        │ yes
        ▼
  escalated push (sourceToken: App installation token or PAT) ──ok──▶ head moved;
        │                                                      CI fires normally (acceptable: head changed, revalidation is required anyway)
        │ rejected (escalation token also lacks workflow write)
        ▼
  park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token" (actionable, not "edits revoked"); not counted toward the 3-strike trail
```
Invariants:
- Same token-in-env pattern as today: `forkPushTokenUrl` keeps `${GH_TOKEN}` in the URL; the escalation only swaps env `GH_TOKEN` and restores it in `finally`. The token never appears in script source or logs.
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- The same classification + escalation applies to the non-fork path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (`js/common/smProvider.js` ~839) for base-repo branches.
- A `validation_failed` park created by a workflows-permission rejection is lifted when the escalated push moves the head (the head now post-dates the park).

## Capability surface (tokens available to the tick)
| Token | Source | Workflow-file write | Push fires CI | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silentToken` | `github.token` | **never** (platform fact) | no | default silent update (core, unchanged) |
| App installation token | `create-github-app-token` (APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY) | only if App has *Workflows: write* | yes | escalation (core) |
| `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT | secret | only with `workflow` scope | yes | escalation fallback when no App (core) |
Excluded: requesting permissions at runtime (impossible); rewriting the merge to skip workflow files (corrupts the branch).

Pinned platform facts (each with +/- test via stderr fixtures): `GITHUB_TOKEN` push touching `.github/workflows/**` is rejected; same push with workflow-capable token succeeds; push not touching workflows succeeds with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Security
- Escalation token is a write token to a **fork** owned by a third party, used only under `maintainerCanModify=true` (existing gate, unchanged).
- Never log the token; stderr tail stays redacted (existing redaction).
- Escalation pushes only the SM-built merge commit of `main` into head — no author content is executed before the push.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- **AC2** — that rejection does **not** increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- **AC3** — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- **AC4** — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- **AC5** — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- **AC6** — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- **AC7** — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

## Test plan
- `UT-1..5` in `js/unit-tests` with stderr fixtures (the exact #1591 line + OAuth-scope variant + unrelated rejection).
- `IT-1/2` SM tick harness with stubbed `cli_execute_command`: first push rejected → second with swapped env succeeds → head moves.
- `REG-1` existing gh-1070 / gh-1074 fork tests unchanged and green.
- Red REG blocks merge even if UT/IT are green.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — no App and PAT lacks `workflow` scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- **E2** — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- **E3** — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- **E4** — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

## Non-goals
- Changing tokens wired in `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml`.
- Auto-unparking PRs parked by genuine maintainer-edit revocation.

## Open questions
- Does the fa App have *Workflows: write*? If not: grant it, or rely on PAT `workflow` scope.

## References
- IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591; gh-1070 AC3, gh-1074 (fork silent-update trail); #687 (silent token); awf#52 (App token).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real

   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization

# gh-1106: SM: fork silent-update must escalate token on 'workflows' permission rejection instead of guest-parking

## Description

## Goal — fork silent-update survives `workflows`-permission rejection (v1)
One sentence: **an approved fork PR whose update-from-main touches `.github/workflows/*` gets its branch updated and merged by the SM instead of parking guest-style forever.**

Today the SM's fork silent-update (`js/smAgent.js` ~2380–2440) pushes the `main` merge into the fork head with `silentToken` (= the caller's `github.token`, `github-actions[bot]`). `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files (no `workflows` permission exists for it, `permissions:` cannot grant it). As soon as `main` has a workflow-file change the fork branch lacks, every push is rejected, `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` counts it as "maintainer edits revoked", and after 3 ticks the PR is parked guest-style with `validation_failed`, which then holds because "the head predates the park event (no new push since)". Deadlock: no push → park holds → no push.

Live case: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591 (fork `YuryBY`, `maintainerCanModify=true`, APPROVED, BEHIND), ticks 2026-10-19 17:16/17:17:
```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> fix/android-dap-home-sandbox (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` without `workflows` permission)
❌ pr-1591 fork silent-update parked guest-style after 3 consecutive push failures (gh-1070 AC3)
🅿️ pr-1591 validation_failed holds — the head predates the park event (no new push since)
```

## Why this framing
- Retracted: "maintainer edits were revoked" — the misdiagnosis gh-1070 AC3 applies to *every* push failure. This rejection is a token-capability fact, not an author decision, and it is deterministic (retrying with the same token can never succeed).
- Retracted: fixing in workflow YAML. `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml` already deliver both `silentToken` and `sourceToken`; the decision belongs to the engine.

## Architecture
Subject of every action = **the fork PR head branch** (`head.repo.full_name`:`head.ref`), never the base repo.

```
silent push (silentToken) ──ok──▶ done (no CI event, as today)
        │ rejected
        ▼ classify stderr tail
  workflows-permission? ──no──▶ existing gh-1070 AC3 trail (unchanged)
        │ yes
        ▼
  escalated push (sourceToken: App installation token or PAT) ──ok──▶ head moved;
        │                                                      CI fires normally (acceptable: head changed, revalidation is required anyway)
        │ rejected (escalation token also lacks workflow write)
        ▼
  park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token" (actionable, not "edits revoked"); not counted toward the 3-strike trail
```
Invariants:
- Same token-in-env pattern as today: `forkPushTokenUrl` keeps `${GH_TOKEN}` in the URL; the escalation only swaps env `GH_TOKEN` and restores it in `finally`. The token never appears in script source or logs.
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- The same classification + escalation applies to the non-fork path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (`js/common/smProvider.js` ~839) for base-repo branches.
- A `validation_failed` park created by a workflows-permission rejection is lifted when the escalated push moves the head (the head now post-dates the park).

## Capability surface (tokens available to the tick)
| Token | Source | Workflow-file write | Push fires CI | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silentToken` | `github.token` | **never** (platform fact) | no | default silent update (core, unchanged) |
| App installation token | `create-github-app-token` (APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY) | only if App has *Workflows: write* | yes | escalation (core) |
| `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT | secret | only with `workflow` scope | yes | escalation fallback when no App (core) |
Excluded: requesting permissions at runtime (impossible); rewriting the merge to skip workflow files (corrupts the branch).

Pinned platform facts (each with +/- test via stderr fixtures): `GITHUB_TOKEN` push touching `.github/workflows/**` is rejected; same push with workflow-capable token succeeds; push not touching workflows succeeds with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Security
- Escalation token is a write token to a **fork** owned by a third party, used only under `maintainerCanModify=true` (existing gate, unchanged).
- Never log the token; stderr tail stays redacted (existing redaction).
- Escalation pushes only the SM-built merge commit of `main` into head — no author content is executed before the push.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- **AC2** — that rejection does **not** increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- **AC3** — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- **AC4** — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- **AC5** — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- **AC6** — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- **AC7** — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

## Test plan
- `UT-1..5` in `js/unit-tests` with stderr fixtures (the exact #1591 line + OAuth-scope variant + unrelated rejection).
- `IT-1/2` SM tick harness with stubbed `cli_execute_command`: first push rejected → second with swapped env succeeds → head moves.
- `REG-1` existing gh-1070 / gh-1074 fork tests unchanged and green.
- Red REG blocks merge even if UT/IT are green.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — no App and PAT lacks `workflow` scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- **E2** — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- **E3** — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- **E4** — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

## Non-goals
- Changing tokens wired in `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml`.
- Auto-unparking PRs parked by genuine maintainer-edit revocation.

## Open questions
- Does the fa App have *Workflows: write*? If not: grant it, or rely on PAT `workflow` scope.

## References
- IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591; gh-1070 AC3, gh-1074 (fork silent-update trail); #687 (silent token); awf#52 (App token).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# gh-1106: SM: fork silent-update must escalate token on 'workflows' permission rejection instead of guest-parking

## Description

## Goal — fork silent-update survives `workflows`-permission rejection (v1)
One sentence: **an approved fork PR whose update-from-main touches `.github/workflows/*` gets its branch updated and merged by the SM instead of parking guest-style forever.**

Today the SM's fork silent-update (`js/smAgent.js` ~2380–2440) pushes the `main` merge into the fork head with `silentToken` (= the caller's `github.token`, `github-actions[bot]`). `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files (no `workflows` permission exists for it, `permissions:` cannot grant it). As soon as `main` has a workflow-file change the fork branch lacks, every push is rejected, `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` counts it as "maintainer edits revoked", and after 3 ticks the PR is parked guest-style with `validation_failed`, which then holds because "the head predates the park event (no new push since)". Deadlock: no push → park holds → no push.

Live case: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591 (fork `YuryBY`, `maintainerCanModify=true`, APPROVED, BEHIND), ticks 2026-10-19 17:16/17:17:
```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> fix/android-dap-home-sandbox (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` without `workflows` permission)
❌ pr-1591 fork silent-update parked guest-style after 3 consecutive push failures (gh-1070 AC3)
🅿️ pr-1591 validation_failed holds — the head predates the park event (no new push since)
```

## Why this framing
- Retracted: "maintainer edits were revoked" — the misdiagnosis gh-1070 AC3 applies to *every* push failure. This rejection is a token-capability fact, not an author decision, and it is deterministic (retrying with the same token can never succeed).
- Retracted: fixing in workflow YAML. `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml` already deliver both `silentToken` and `sourceToken`; the decision belongs to the engine.

## Architecture
Subject of every action = **the fork PR head branch** (`head.repo.full_name`:`head.ref`), never the base repo.

```
silent push (silentToken) ──ok──▶ done (no CI event, as today)
        │ rejected
        ▼ classify stderr tail
  workflows-permission? ──no──▶ existing gh-1070 AC3 trail (unchanged)
        │ yes
        ▼
  escalated push (sourceToken: App installation token or PAT) ──ok──▶ head moved;
        │                                                      CI fires normally (acceptable: head changed, revalidation is required anyway)
        │ rejected (escalation token also lacks workflow write)
        ▼
  park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token" (actionable, not "edits revoked"); not counted toward the 3-strike trail
```
Invariants:
- Same token-in-env pattern as today: `forkPushTokenUrl` keeps `${GH_TOKEN}` in the URL; the escalation only swaps env `GH_TOKEN` and restores it in `finally`. The token never appears in script source or logs.
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- The same classification + escalation applies to the non-fork path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (`js/common/smProvider.js` ~839) for base-repo branches.
- A `validation_failed` park created by a workflows-permission rejection is lifted when the escalated push moves the head (the head now post-dates the park).

## Capability surface (tokens available to the tick)
| Token | Source | Workflow-file write | Push fires CI | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silentToken` | `github.token` | **never** (platform fact) | no | default silent update (core, unchanged) |
| App installation token | `create-github-app-token` (APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY) | only if App has *Workflows: write* | yes | escalation (core) |
| `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT | secret | only with `workflow` scope | yes | escalation fallback when no App (core) |
Excluded: requesting permissions at runtime (impossible); rewriting the merge to skip workflow files (corrupts the branch).

Pinned platform facts (each with +/- test via stderr fixtures): `GITHUB_TOKEN` push touching `.github/workflows/**` is rejected; same push with workflow-capable token succeeds; push not touching workflows succeeds with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Security
- Escalation token is a write token to a **fork** owned by a third party, used only under `maintainerCanModify=true` (existing gate, unchanged).
- Never log the token; stderr tail stays redacted (existing redaction).
- Escalation pushes only the SM-built merge commit of `main` into head — no author content is executed before the push.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- **AC2** — that rejection does **not** increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- **AC3** — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- **AC4** — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- **AC5** — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- **AC6** — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- **AC7** — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

## Test plan
- `UT-1..5` in `js/unit-tests` with stderr fixtures (the exact #1591 line + OAuth-scope variant + unrelated rejection).
- `IT-1/2` SM tick harness with stubbed `cli_execute_command`: first push rejected → second with swapped env succeeds → head moves.
- `REG-1` existing gh-1070 / gh-1074 fork tests unchanged and green.
- Red REG blocks merge even if UT/IT are green.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — no App and PAT lacks `workflow` scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- **E2** — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- **E3** — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- **E4** — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

## Non-goals
- Changing tokens wired in `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml`.
- Auto-unparking PRs parked by genuine maintainer-edit revocation.

## Open questions
- Does the fa App have *Workflows: write*? If not: grant it, or rely on PAT `workflow` scope.

## References
- IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591; gh-1070 AC3, gh-1074 (fork silent-update trail); #687 (silent token); awf#52 (App token).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash

     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain

The ticket says:
- AC1 — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- AC2 — that rejection does not increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- AC3 — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).

Architecture:
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`.

- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- Park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token", not counted toward the 3-strike trail.

Edge cases:
- E1 — no App and PAT lacks workflow scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- E2 — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- E3 — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.

# gh-1106: SM: fork silent-update must escalate token on 'workflows' permission rejection instead of guest-parking

## Description

## Goal — fork silent-update survives `workflows`-permission rejection (v1)
One sentence: **an approved fork PR whose update-from-main touches `.github/workflows/*` gets its branch updated and merged by the SM instead of parking guest-style forever.**

Today the SM's fork silent-update (`js/smAgent.js` ~2380–2440) pushes the `main` merge into the fork head with `silentToken` (= the caller's `github.token`, `github-actions[bot]`). `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files (no `workflows` permission exists for it, `permissions:` cannot grant it). As soon as `main` has a workflow-file change the fork branch lacks, every push is rejected, `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure` counts it as "maintainer edits revoked", and after 3 ticks the PR is parked guest-style with `validation_failed`, which then holds because "the head predates the park event (no new push since)". Deadlock: no push → park holds → no push.

Live case: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591 (fork `YuryBY`, `maintainerCanModify=true`, APPROVED, BEHIND), ticks 2026-10-19 17:16/17:17:
```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> fix/android-dap-home-sandbox (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` without `workflows` permission)
❌ pr-1591 fork silent-update parked guest-style after 3 consecutive push failures (gh-1070 AC3)
🅿️ pr-1591 validation_failed holds — the head predates the park event (no new push since)
```

## Why this framing
- Retracted: "maintainer edits were revoked" — the misdiagnosis gh-1070 AC3 applies to *every* push failure. This rejection is a token-capability fact, not an author decision, and it is deterministic (retrying with the same token can never succeed).
- Retracted: fixing in workflow YAML. `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml` already deliver both `silentToken` and `sourceToken`; the decision belongs to the engine.

## Architecture
Subject of every action = **the fork PR head branch** (`head.repo.full_name`:`head.ref`), never the base repo.

```
silent push (silentToken) ──ok──▶ done (no CI event, as today)
        │ rejected
        ▼ classify stderr tail
  workflows-permission? ──no──▶ existing gh-1070 AC3 trail (unchanged)
        │ yes
        ▼
  escalated push (sourceToken: App installation token or PAT) ──ok──▶ head moved;
        │                                                      CI fires normally (acceptable: head changed, revalidation is required anyway)
        │ rejected (escalation token also lacks workflow write)
        ▼
  park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token" (actionable, not "edits revoked"); not counted toward the 3-strike trail
```
Invariants:
- Same token-in-env pattern as today: `forkPushTokenUrl` keeps `${GH_TOKEN}` in the URL; the escalation only swaps env `GH_TOKEN` and restores it in `finally`. The token never appears in script source or logs.
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- The same classification + escalation applies to the non-fork path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (`js/common/smProvider.js` ~839) for base-repo branches.
- A `validation_failed` park created by a workflows-permission rejection is lifted when the escalated push moves the head (the head now post-dates the park).

## Capability surface (tokens available to the tick)
| Token | Source | Workflow-file write | Push fires CI | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silentToken` | `github.token` | **never** (platform fact) | no | default silent update (core, unchanged) |
| App installation token | `create-github-app-token` (APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY) | only if App has *Workflows: write* | yes | escalation (core) |
| `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT | secret | only with `workflow` scope | yes | escalation fallback when no App (core) |
Excluded: requesting permissions at runtime (impossible); rewriting the merge to skip workflow files (corrupts the branch).

Pinned platform facts (each with +/- test via stderr fixtures): `GITHUB_TOKEN` push touching `.github/workflows/**` is rejected; same push with workflow-capable token succeeds; push not touching workflows succeeds with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Security
- Escalation token is a write token to a **fork** owned by a third party, used only under `maintainerCanModify=true` (existing gate, unchanged).
- Never log the token; stderr tail stays redacted (existing redaction).
- Escalation pushes only the SM-built merge commit of `main` into head — no author content is executed before the push.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- **AC2** — that rejection does **not** increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- **AC3** — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- **AC4** — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- **AC5** — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- **AC6** — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- **AC7** — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

## Test plan
- `UT-1..5` in `js/unit-tests` with stderr fixtures (the exact #1591 line + OAuth-scope variant + unrelated rejection).
- `IT-1/2` SM tick harness with stubbed `cli_execute_command`: first push rejected → second with swapped env succeeds → head moves.
- `REG-1` existing gh-1070 / gh-1074 fork tests unchanged and green.
- Red REG blocks merge even if UT/IT are green.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — no App and PAT lacks `workflow` scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- **E2** — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- **E3** — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- **E4** — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

## Non-goals
- Changing tokens wired in `machine-sm.yml` / `factory-sm.yml`.
- Auto-unparking PRs parked by genuine maintainer-edit revocation.

## Open questions
- Does the fa App have *Workflows: write*? If not: grant it, or rely on PAT `workflow` scope.

## References
- IstiN/flutter_agent_harness#1591; gh-1070 AC3, gh-1074 (fork silent-update trail); #687 (silent token); awf#52 (App token).
