# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

- AC1 — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- AC2 — that rejection does not increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- AC3 — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- AC4 — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- AC5 — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- AC6 — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- AC7 — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

Architecture:
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`.
- Escalated push uses `sourceToken` (App installation token or PAT).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- Park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token", not counted toward the 3-strike trail.

Edge cases:
- E1 — no App and PAT lacks workflow scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- E2 — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- E3 — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- E4 — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

# Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'

# Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

Found `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` in smProvider.js around line 838-855. This is the base-repo path — used by merge cadence ("Silent refresh of an armed PR"). It calls `gh pr update-branch <prNumber> --repo <full>` with `GH_TOKEN` set to `silentToken`.

The ticket says:
- AC1 — workflows-permission rejection with `silentToken` triggers exactly one escalated push with `sourceToken` in the same tick (UT-1, IT-1).
- AC2 — that rejection does not increment the gh-1070 failure trail and does not park guest-style (UT-2).
- AC3 — if escalation also fails with the same class, the PR parks with a distinct reason/marker naming the missing token capability (UT-3).
- AC4 — after a successful escalated push the `validation_failed` hold is released by the existing "new push since park" rule and CI is dispatched (IT-2).
- AC5 — non-workflows rejections keep today's behavior byte-identical (REG-1).
- AC6 — same behavior on the base-repo path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (UT-4).
- AC7 — `GH_TOKEN` env is restored after escalation even on exception (UT-5).

Architecture:
- Classifier is a pure function `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`.
- Escalated push uses `sourceToken` (App installation token or PAT).
- One escalated attempt per PR per tick.
- Park with a DISTINCT reason "update needs workflow-write token", not counted toward the 3-strike trail.

Edge cases:
- E1 — no App and PAT lacks workflow scope → AC3 park, one marker, no infinite retries.
- E2 — author disables maintainer edits mid-flight → old gh-1070 path (different stderr).
- E3 — dry-run: logs the planned escalation, no push.
- E4 — stderr truncated before the marker phrase → treated as generic (safe default).

Key areas to change:
1. `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — add `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` pure classifier.
2. `js/smAgent.js` fork silent-update chain — on failure, classify the stderr tail:
  - If workflows-permission rejection → escalate once: swap env GH_TOKEN to sourceToken (RUN_JOB_PARAMS.sourceToken) and retry the push; if that fails too with the same class → park with distinct reason "update needs workflow-write token", one marker, NOT counted in the 3-strike trail.
  - Otherwise → existing gh-1070 trail unchanged.
3. `js/common/smProvider.js` `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` — same classification + escalation for base-repo branches.

Note the token-in-env pattern: `forkPushTokenUrl` keeps `${GH_TOKEN}` in the URL; the escalation only swaps env `GH_TOKEN` and restores it in `finally`.

244:          "localAction": "update_branch",
249:          "description": "HEAD-CHANGE PARK RESET (gh-994, owner reframe 2026-10-17, live fa #156/#1563 - 4 manual label deletions in one day): when the park comment records the punished head sha ('parked-head: <sha>') and the current headRefOid DIFFERS, the label is removed UNCONDITIONALLY - no actor, park-time or verdict probes. Every head-mutation source resets the park: kicker push, machine rework-leg push, operator push, silent merge-main update; guests and machine PRs alike. A genuinely red new head is re-parked by the validation path one cycle later. Audit: machine log 'park-reset: <pr> head <old>-><new>' only, no PR comment. Sticky-park RESET for NON-BEHIND heads (dmtools-agents, live fa 2026-10-03): the human-push unpark probe lives inside update_branch, but silent-update-behind only matches mergeState BEHIND — a guest PR whose fix commit lands on the SAME base (not behind) NEVER runs the RESET and the park outlives any human push (live: vendor pushed 16:01 to five parked approved PRs; 2h later not one label cleared, the whole approved FIFO frozen). There's a pattern: `recordNoRefBookeeping` reads pr comments, counts markers via `triggerFailMarks`, dedupes via the label snapshot + `tickParkedRecorded`.

Now, important design decision for AC3 park dedupe. The label snapshot guard `if ((item.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') !== -1) return;` is the established idempotency approach. For the gh-1106 park, the flow per tick:

1. Tick N: silent push → workflows rejection → escalate (sourceToken) → also rejected (workflows class) → park (label add + distinct comment with parked-head). `validation_failed` label added → but ticket.labels is the tick-START snapshot, so within the same tick nothing else re-parks. Next tick (N+1): the snapshot now has validation_failed... 
2. Tick N+1: park-reset rule routes the parked PR through update_branch. The gh-994 head-change RESET probe: head unchanged → park holds. Fork gate: maintainerCanModify=true → refresh attempt → silent push rejected (workflows) → escalate → rejected → park again?

If I guard the park on the label snapshot (like parkNonEditableFork), tick N+1 posts nothing (label present in snapshot) but STILL performs the escalation attempt (retry — self-healing if the token capability is later granted). That matches "no infinite retries" in the sense of no unbounded marker trail: one park comment + one marker; retries continue silently every tick, same as gh-1070's every-tick retry contract ("the retry itself stays every-tick (self-healing)").

Hmm wait — actually, does the escalation continue every tick? The gh-1070 comment says the retry stays every-tick. For the workflows class the ticket says "One escalated attempt per PR per tick" — so yes, one per tick. And "no infinite retries" (E1) — I read this as: no growing trail, no crash loop of multiple escalations per tick, one marker. The park+silent-retry-every-tick is the same liveness contract as today.

OK here's a subtlety though — should the SILENT push still be attempted every tick when we KNOW it will be rejected (deterministic)? The silent push is the default path (core, unchanged) — the rejection is how we discover main has workflow changes. Attempting it first is how we classify. Keep it (AC5 byte-identical non-workflows behavior, and the silent-first probe is the classification source).

Now — where does `DRY` fit (E3: dry-run logs the planned escalation, no push)? In the escalation: if DRY, log the planned escalation and skip the push. Return false (no head move) and don't park (dry runs park nothing — check how parkNonEditableFork guards: `if (unparkedThisPass || DRY || ...) return;`). For dry: log '[dry] escalation planned' and return without parking. But hmm — if DRY and the silent push failed... actually in DRY mode, does silent update even run? Let me check how DRY guards silentUpdateBranch... Looking at the update_branch flow at line ~2913: `refreshHeadSilent()` is called unconditionally (no DRY guard visible). Let me check if cli_execute_command is a no-op under DRY... Actually the SM's DRY mode probably still executes read-only commands but the dispatchCiWorkflow has an explicit DRY guard. Hmm, but silentUpdateBranch RUNS the clone+push — a push is a side effect! Let me search for DRY handling around the update branch rule.

Looking at the flow at 2913-2921: `refreshHeadSilent(); console.log('✅ branch silently updated')` — no DRY guard. Hmm, that means in DRY the push happens?! Wait — maybe the update_branch action returns early under DRY. Let me check line 1378: `if (DRY) { console.log('\n══ [LOCAL·DRY] ...') }` — the rule execution continues after that log. And dispatchCiWorkflow has an explicit DRY guard. But silentUpdateBranch pushes for real in DRY? That seems inconsistent, but the live bug comment at 2542 says a DRY tick really dispatched CI — meaning silent update DID run side effects in DRY and that was known/acceptable? Now, what about "One escalated attempt per PR per tick"? The update_branch rule may process the same PR... each rule processes distinct items, but BOTH silent-update-behind and park-reset rules could match the same PR in one tick! silent-update-behind excludes ai_validating only; park-reset requires validation_failed. Disjoint label sets (one has validation_failed, the other doesn't... well silent-update-behind has notLabels validation_failed!). Hmm: silent-update-behind: {type: pr, notLabels: [ai_validating], mergeState: BEHIND} — a parked PR (validation_failed + BEHIND) matches BOTH rules. The park-reset rule runs first (rule order?), then silent-update-behind → the PR is processed TWICE per tick → two silent-update attempts + potentially two escalations per tick!

Wait, but is that true today for the 3-strike trail? Each rule pass records a failure marker per attempt... the counting reads markers from PR comments (silentUpdateFailureCount reads all markers) so two attempts per tick → 2 markers per tick → parks after 2 ticks instead of 3. Hmm, that's existing behavior, not my concern.

For gh-1106 "one escalated attempt per PR per tick": after the FIRST rule's escalation fails and parks (label added to GitHub but the snapshot still lacks it), the SECOND rule's pass would see the PR again (items re-queried per rule — `opts.github.items` may be a function called per rule). The gh-922 `tickParkedRecorded` mechanism handles exactly this: "a sibling rule already recorded this PR earlier in the SAME tick — the stale label snapshot cannot see its park". I can use a similar tick-scoped guard for the escalation: `tickWorkflowEscalation[item.prNumber] = true` set when an escalation is attempted; subsequent attempts in the same tick skip escalation. But wait — if the escalation SUCCEEDED in the first pass, the head moved, and the second pass's silent push would succeed (head now contains main — the up-to-date clause exits 0). So no escalation needed. The guard only matters when escalation fails/parks. Good — a tick-scoped `escalatedThisTick` map mirrors `tickParkedRecorded`.

Hmm, but is that over-enginering? The live case: PR parked (validation_failed) + BEHIND → matches both rules. Order in sm.json: park-reset is rule id at line 24-ish, silent-update-behind at 262 — park-reset comes first. Park-reset pass: parked head unchanged → holds... then fork gate → refresh → rejection → escalation → fail → park (comment). Then silent-update-behind pass: re-queried items — the githubSource re-queries? If the source re-fetches open PRs (dropOpenPrsCache?), the label may already show validation_failed... The `unparkedThisPass` and `parkedRedHeadThisPass` machinery exists because of these same-tick multi-rule flows. Without the per-tick escalation guard, the same PR gets TWO escalations in one tick, violating AC1's "exactly one escalated push ... in the same tick". So yes — add the tick-scoped guard. Mirror `tickParkedRecorded` naming: `tickWorkflowEscalation = {}` reset per tick.

Every head-mutation source resets the park: kicker push, machine rework-leg push, operator push, silent merge-main update; guests and machine PRs alike. A genuinely red new head is re-parked by the validation path one cycle later. Audit: machine log 'park-reset: <pr> head <old>-><new>' only, no PR comment. Sticky-park RESET for NON-BEHIND heads (dmtools-agents, live fa 2026-10-03): the human-push unpark probe lives inside update_branch, but silent-update-behind only matches mergeState BEHIND — a guest PR whose fix commit lands on the SAME base (not behind) NEVER runs the RESET and the park outlives any human push (live: vendor pushed 16:01 to five parked approved PRs; 2h later not one label cleared, the whole approved FIFO frozen). This rule routes every parked non-validating PR through update_branch's RESET probe regardless of merge state: a NON-machine SUBSTANTIVE push NEWER than the newest park event clears the label — the probe walks back past machine-authored merges of main to the last substantive commit: a bot merge BURIES the retrigger, never replaces it (dmtools-agents#681, live fa#1213 2026-10-03 22:56–23:10: retrigger 7ecf11d7 buried by bot merge b3f9c6b5 before the next tick, the old head-keyed probe declined and the park survived 4 real ticks); then validate-armed picks the PR up on a later pass (this rule never dispatches CI itself); machine pushes and stale heads keep the park (fail closed). # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

content.text:
/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

blocks.text:
/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

blocks.text:
/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

# Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).

There's a pattern: `recordNoRefBookeeping` reads pr comments, counts markers via `triggerFailMarks`, dedupes via the label snapshot + `tickParkedRecorded`.

Now, important design decision for AC3 park dedupe. The label snapshot guard `if ((item.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') !== -1) return;` is the established idempotency approach. For the gh-1106 park, the flow per tick:

1. Tick N: silent push → workflows rejection → escalate (sourceToken) → also rejected (workflows class) → park (label add + distinct comment with parked-head). `validation_failed` label added → but ticket.labels is the tick-START snapshot, so within the same tick nothing else re-parks. Next tick (N+1): the snapshot now has validation_failed... 
2. Tick N+1: park-reset rule routes the parked PR through update_branch. The gh-994 head-change RESET probe: head unchanged → park holds. Fork gate: maintainerCanModify=true → refresh attempt → silent push rejected (workflows) → escalate → rejected → park again?

If I guard the park on the label snapshot (like parkNonEditableFork), tick N+1 posts nothing (label present in snapshot) but STILL performs the escalation attempt (retry — self-healing if the token capability is later granted). That matches "no infinite retries" in the sense of no unbounded marker trail: one park comment + one marker; retries continue silently every tick, same as gh-1070's every-tick retry contract ("the retry itself stays every-tick (self-healing)").

Hmm wait — actually, does the escalation continue every tick? The gh-1070 comment says the retry stays every-tick. For the workflows class the ticket says "One escalated attempt per PR per tick" — so yes, one per tick. And "no infinite retries" (E1) — I read this as: no growing trail, no crash loop of multiple escalations per tick, one marker. The park+silent-retry-every-tick is the same liveness contract as today.

OK here's a subtlety though — should the SILENT push still be attempted every tick when we KNOW it will be rejected (deterministic)? The silent push is the default path (core, unchanged) — the rejection is how we discover main has workflow changes. Attempting it first is how we classify. Keep it (AC5 byte-identical non-workflows behavior, and the silent-first probe is the classification source).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

Now, important design decision for AC3 park dedupe. The label snapshot guard `if ((item.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') !== -1) return;` is the established idempotency approach. For the gh-1106 park, the flow per tick:

1. Tick N: silent push → workflows rejection → escalate (sourceToken) → also rejected (workflows class) → park (label add + distinct comment with parked-head). `validation_failed` label added → but ticket.labels is the tick-START snapshot, so within the same tick nothing else re-parks. Next tick (N+1): the snapshot now has validation_failed... 
2. Tick N+1: park-reset rule routes the parked PR through update_branch. The gh-994 head-change RESET probe: head unchanged → park holds. Fork gate: maintainerCanModify=true → refresh attempt → silent push rejected (workflows) → escalate → rejected → park again?

If I guard the park on the label snapshot (like parkNonEditableFork), tick N+1 posts nothing (label present in snapshot) but STILL performs the escalation attempt (retry — self-healing if the token capability is later granted). That matches "no infinite retries" in the sense of no unbounded marker trail: one park comment + one marker; retries continue silently every tick, same as gh-1070's every-tick retry contract ("the retry itself stays every-tick (self-healing)").

Hmm wait — actually, does the escalation continue every tick? The gh-1070 comment says the retry stays every-tick. For the workflows class the ticket says "One escalated attempt per PR per tick" — so yes, one per tick. And "no infinite retries" (E1) — I read this as: no growing trail, no crash loop of multiple escalations per tick, one marker. The park+silent-retry-every-tick is the same liveness contract as today.

OK here's a subtlety though — should the SILENT push still be attempted every tick when we KNOW it will be rejected (deterministic)? The silent push is the default path (core, unchanged) — the rejection is how we discover main has workflow changes. Attempting it first is how we classify. Keep it (AC5 byte-identical non-workflows behavior, and the silent-first probe is the classification source).

Now — where does `DRY` fit (E3: dry-run logs the planned escalation, no push)? In the escalation: if DRY, log the planned escalation and skip the push. Return false (no head move) and don't park (dry runs park nothing — check how parkNonEditableFork guards: `if (unparkedThisPass || DRY || ...) return;`).
