/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

blocks.text:
/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

Good. Now let me write the plan concretely.

## Implementation plan

### A. `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (pure, tested)
1. `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` — matches the GitHub refusal stem:
  - `/refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow/i`
  - `/refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow [^\n]*without [`']workflow[`'] scope/i`
  Per ticket: matches both pinned phrasings. E4: anything without the phrase → false (empty/null → false).
   
  Implementation: one combined regex — actually two separate patterns ORed. Ticket literally says "matches `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow` and `refusing to allow an OAuth App ... without \`workflow\` scope`". Two regexes:
  - `WORKFLOW_APP_RE = /refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow/i`
  - `WORKFLOW_OAUTH_RE = /refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow [^\n]*without [`"']workflow[`"'] scope/i`
   
  Hmm — the OAuth actual message: "refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow `build.yml` without `workflow` scope". So `without \`workflow\` scope` follows. My second regex: `/refusing to allow an OAuth App .*without [`'\u0060]workflow[`'\u0060] scope/i` — backtick in a JS regex literal is fine (no escaping needed). Let me be careful with quotes in my file write — backticks are fine in GralJS as regex chars.

2. `workflowWriteParkLine(headSha, atIso)` — distinct marker line: 
  `'🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) — update needs a workflow-write token at ' + atIso` plus the parked-head rides separately like recordNoRefBokeping ('\nparked-head: ' + sha). For dedupe, I'll scan comments for `/🔐 workflow-write park \(gh-1106\)/` + `parked-head: <sha>`. Simpler dedupe: one regex `WORKFLOW_PARK_MARKER_RE = /🔐 workflow-write park \(gh-1106\)[^\n]*parked-head: ([0-9a-f]{7,40})/` — hmm, ordering: marker line then parked-head on separate lines complicates the single regex. Put the parked-head ON the marker line:
   
  `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) — update needs a workflow-write token at <iso> · parked-head: <sha>`
   
  One line, greppable, dedupe-able. And a pure helper `workflowWriteParkMarked(bodies, headSha)` → true when any body carries the marker for that head. (Mirors ghostGuardMarks/triggerFailMarks style.)

### B. `js/smAgent.js` fork path (UT-1..5, IT-1/2)
1. Module scope: `var tickWorkflowEscalations = null;` + reset in `action()` next to tickParkedRecorded.
2. In the fork block:
  - `forkSilentUpdateBranchTracked(branchName, forkFull)` catch → read tail → classify:
    - workflows class → `escalateForkSilentUpdate(branchName, forkFull, tail)`:
      - DRY → log planned escalation (E3), no push, no park.
      - already escalated this tick (map guard) → log defer, no park (defer to next tick), no trail.
      - no sourceToken → E1 park distinct (one marker), no trail.
      - else swap env GH_TOKEN → sourceToken (set_env_variable), re-run `forkSilentUpdateBranch` with a fresh stderr file:
        - success → restore env (finally), head moved → done (log 'silent update escalated — head moved'), no trail, no park. Optionally: cancelStaleAfterRefreshUb already runs in the caller after refreshHeadSilent? NO — wait. The caller does:
        ```
        try {
            refreshHeadSilent();
            console.log(' ✅ ... branch silently updated (no CI)');
            cancelStaleAfterRefreshUb();
        } catch (e) { '❌ update_branch failed' }
        ```
        Hmm — actually refreshHeadSilent is called and if it THROWS, the outer catch logs 'update_branch failed'. My escalation lives INSIDE forkSilentUpdateBranchTracked; if the escalated push succeeds, the function RETURNS NORMALLY → caller logs '✅ branch silently updated' and runs cancelStaleAfterRefreshUb (cancels stale runs on the OLD head — correct, the head moved!). 
      - escalated push fails:

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

blocks.text:
/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

blocks.text:
/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

/**
 * SM Provider — SCM-agnostic I/O for the machine-loop watchdog
 * (machineSmAgent.js).
 *
 * The watchdog's decision core is pure state → actions; this module is the
 * only place that talks to a forge. Provider selection mirrors scm.js:
 *
 *     var provider = createSmProvider({
 *         scm:    { provider: 'github' },           // 'github' | 'gitlab'
 *         repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' }
 *     });
 *
 * Everything goes through the unified snake_case tool surface (github_* /
 * gitlab_* MCP tools via the dmtools JS bridge) — the same abstraction the
 * rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).

Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 4757 tests — includes new gh-1106 suites
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_validationLiveness.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
- UT-1..5 / IT-1: fork lane tests in `test_smAgent.js` ("fork silent-update workflow-write escalation (gh-1106)"); UT-4 in `test_smProvider.js`; REG-1 pins non-workflows failures byte-identical (no env swap, trail unchanged).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[silent push — silentToken] -->|ok| D[done — no CI event]
  P -->|rejected| C{isWorkflowsPermissionRejection?}
  C -->|no| T[gh-1070 3-strike trail — unchanged]
  C -->|yes| E[escalated push — GH_TOKEN:=sourceToken]
  E -->|ok| M[head moved — gh-994 park reset, validation re-dispatch]
  E -->|workflows refusal again| PK[park: workflow-write park marker — not on the trail]
```

</details>

Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

```bash

dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).

Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).

```bash

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 4757 tests — includes new gh-1106 suites
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_validationLiveness.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
- UT-1..5 / IT-1: fork lane tests in `test_smAgent.js` ("fork silent-update workflow-write escalation (gh-1106)"); UT-4 in `test_smProvider.js`; REG-1 pins non-workflows failures byte-identical (no env swap, trail unchanged).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[silent push — silentToken] -->|ok| D[done — no CI event]
  P -->|rejected| C{isWorkflowsPermissionRejection?}
  C -->|no| T[gh-1070 3-strike trail — unchanged]
  C -->|yes| E[escalated push — GH_TOKEN:=sourceToken]
  E -->|ok| M[head moved — gh-994 park reset, validation re-dispatch]
  E -->|workflows refusal again| PK[park: workflow-write park marker — not on the trail]
```

</details>

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 4757 tests — includes new gh-1106 suites
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_validationLiveness.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
- UT-1..5 / IT-1: fork lane tests in `test_smAgent.js` ("fork silent-update workflow-write escalation (gh-1106)"); UT-4 in `test_smProvider.js`; REG-1 pins non-workflows failures byte-identical (no env swap, trail unchanged).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[silent push — silentToken] -->|ok| D[done — no CI event]
  P -->|rejected| C{isWorkflowsPermissionRejection?}
  C -->|no| T[gh-1070 3-strike trail — unchanged]
  C -->|yes| E[escalated push — GH_TOKEN:=sourceToken]
  E -->|ok| M[head moved — gh-994 park reset, validation re-dispatch]
  E -->|workflows refusal again| PK[park: workflow-write park marker — not on the trail]
```

</details>

Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

flowchart TD

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 4757 tests — includes new gh-1106 suites
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_validationLiveness.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[silent push — silentToken] -->|ok| D[done — no CI event]
  P -->|rejected| C{isWorkflowsPermissionRejection?}
  C -->|no| T[gh-1070 3-strike trail — unchanged]
  C -->|yes| E[escalated push — GH_TOKEN:=sourceToken]
  E -->|ok| M[head moved — gh-994 park reset, validation re-dispatch]
  E -->|workflows refusal again| PK[park: workflow-write park marker — not on the trail]
```

</details>

Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 4757 tests — includes new gh-1106 suites
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_validationLiveness.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  P -->|rejected| C{isWorkflowsPermissionRejection?}
  C -->|no| T[gh-1070 3-strike trail — unchanged]

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 4757 tests — includes new gh-1106 suites
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_validationLiveness.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[silent push — silentToken] -->|ok| D[done — no CI event]
  P -->|rejected| C{isWorkflowsPermissionRejection?}
  C -->|no| T[gh-1070 3-strike trail — unchanged]
  C -->|yes| E[escalated push — GH_TOKEN:=sourceToken]
  E -->|ok| M[head moved — gh-994 park reset, validation re-dispatch]
  E -->|workflows refusal again| PK[park: workflow-write park marker — not on the trail]
```

</details>

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).
- DRY ticks log the planned escalation and push/park nothing (E3). `machine-sm.yml`/`factory-sm.yml` already deliver `sourceToken` — no workflow wiring changed; open question (App `Workflows: write` grant vs PAT `workflow` scope) stays an operator decision, both shapes are supported.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 4757 tests — includes new gh-1106 suites
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_validationLiveness.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json && dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
- UT-1..5 / IT-1: fork lane tests in `test_smAgent.js` ("fork silent-update workflow-write escalation (gh-1106)"); UT-4 in `test_smProvider.js`; REG-1 pins non-workflows failures byte-identical (no env swap, trail unchanged).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[silent push — silentToken] -->|ok| D[done — no CI event]
  P -->|rejected| C{isWorkflowsPermissionRejection?}
  C -->|no| T[gh-1070 3-strike trail — unchanged]
  C -->|yes| E[escalated push — GH_TOKEN:=sourceToken]
  E -->|ok| M[head moved — gh-994 park reset, validation re-dispatch]
  E -->|workflows refusal again| PK[park: workflow-write park marker — not on the trail]
```

</details>

content.text:
### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).

Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).

### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7). One escalated attempt per PR per tick via a `tickWorkflowEscalations` claim (park-reset + silent-update-behind can both route a parked fork in one pass).
- Distinct park marker `🔐 workflow-write park (gh-1106) … parked-head: <sha>` — one per parked head (comment-deduped), parseable by the existing gh-994 head-change reset, so the first successful escalation (or any head-moving push) lifts the park and CI re-enters via the standard lanes (AC3, AC4).
- Same classify+escalate applied to the base-repo provider path `_ghSilentUpdateBranch` (optional 5th `escalationToken` arg; without it the refusal surfaces a distinct error naming the capability gap) (AC6, E1).

Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### What changed
Fork silent-update now survives `workflows`-permission rejections: the refusal is classified from the captured stderr tail, escalated **once** with the workflow-write token (`jobParams.sourceToken`), and only a second refusal parks the PR — with a distinct "needs a workflow-write token" reason, never on the gh-1070 "edits revoked" 3-strike trail.

### Key decisions
- Pure classifier `isWorkflowsPermissionRejection(stderrTail)` in `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — matches the GitHub App form (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow …`) and the OAuth/PAT form (`… without 'workflow' scope`); anything else (protected-branch hooks, real edit revocations, truncated tails) stays generic (AC5, E2, E4).
- Escalation reuses the identical git chain — only env `GH_TOKEN` is swapped to `sourceToken` and restored in `finally` (even on exception); the token never enters script source or logs (AC1, AC7).
